newsitem.title: USA: NASA delays start of Hubble spacewalk.
newsitem.headline: NASA delays start of Hubble spacewalk.

text.p: NASA put on hold the first of four spacewalks to service the Hubble Space Telescope on Thursday after one the observatory's solar panels swung around unexpectedly.
Astronauts Mark Lee and Steve Smith were preparing to leave the shuttle's airlock to install two new scientific instruments aboard the telescope.
The spacewalk had been due to start at 10 p.m. EST (0300 GMT on Friday), about one hour and 20 minutes ahead of the original schedule.

Flight controllers believed the right-hand array was hit by air venting from the airlock compartment, which is located in the shuttle's cargo bay. The depressurization was halted and the two astronauts remained inside the airlock.

"We saw something real unusual," Discovery crewman Joe Tanner informed mission control. "The ... array slewed from horizontal to vertical and then about halfway back to horizontal." The 40-ft (12-metre) long array swung around within five seconds, he said.

"That must have been very dramatic," mission control's Jeff Hoffman said. Mission control informed the crew they were checking the telescope for damage and were devising a new method of depressurizing the airlock without affecting the telescope's solar panels.
